reasons: The idea is new and worth compute. No prior report holds FX across a weekend on purpose. The flow atlas used windows of at most 8 hours on single weekdays, and its series leave out Monday's weekend gap. gap_cnyfix measured Monday gap fills, not the Friday-to-Monday return. prior_fx_carry rebalanced monthly. So this is not a duplicate. The sample is about 410 trades per market in design, the first adequately powered test in three cycles, and the weekday-overnight control with matched hold lengths is good design (Fri 16:00->Mon 07:00 is about 15 trading hours, the same as Mon 16:00->Tue 07:00; Fri 20:00->Mon 00:00 is about 4, the same as Mon 20:00->Tue 00:00).

One claim in the rationale is false: 'paid twice: the weekend swap (three days of positive carry)'. Spot FX settles T+2, so the triple rollover falls on Wednesday, not Friday. The engine models it the same way (edge/engine/costs.py: 'one night of interest per 17:00 New York rollover held, three on Wednesday'), and the flow atlas NOTES show the Dukascopy price itself drops by about the interest differential at each 17:00 NY rollover, 3x on Wednesday ('the swap pays it back, so there is nothing to trade'). A Friday-to-Monday hold therefore crosses one 1x rollover, the same as the Monday control. Net carry is about zero minus the 1% markup in both arms. The weekend premium has to come from price alone, and the expectation '4-8 pips including swap' must be restated as price-only.

The cost estimate is too low. 'One spread plus slippage (0.9 + 0.4 pips) ... about 0.01 R' uses the all-hours median spread. Entry at Friday 20:00 UTC is the last 1-2 hours before the weekly close, when AUDJPY/NZDJPY spreads widen several-fold, and the 00:00 UTC Monday exit sits close to the thin Sunday-open book. The $7/lot commission adds about another pip on the JPY crosses. A realistic round trip is 3-4 pips, or about 0.025-0.03 R at sl_atr 1.5 and about 0.015 R at 3.0. That is the same size as the expected premium of 0.02-0.06 R, so the 1.5x gate is a real threat and the 2x soft gate probably fails at sl_atr 1.5. The control arm trades at normal mid-week spreads, so it carries lower costs than the Friday arm. That biases the comparison against the hypothesis, which is conservative and acceptable, but the cost gap should be reported.

The exit rule as written exits one hour early. 'Let X be the first H1 bar whose close time is at or after exit_utc ... exit_long[X - 1]' picks X = the 06:00 bar for a 07:00 exit (it closes at 07:00), so the position closes at that bar's open, 06:00. The entry rule (S = last bar closing at or before entry_utc, fill at the next open = entry_utc) is correct; the exit rule is inconsistent with it.

Kill rule (4), 'check period positive with 2020 removed', must not replace the hard gate. The weekend crash tail (2015-08-24, 2020-03-09/16, 2024-08-05 were all Monday-Asia events) is exactly the risk this premium is supposed to pay for. Dropping the crash year flatters the result. Both conditions must hold: check positive with all years (hard gate) and with 2020 removed.

Overfit risk is low. The hypothesis arms form a 2x2 family of session-anchored times (US afternoon de-risking vs last hour; Tokyo vs London re-risking) and come from theory. sl_atr barely binds: a 1.5-3 x ATR20 stop is rarely touched in about 4-15 trading hours, so it mostly rescales R and adds almost no selection freedom. The control is pre-registered with a numeric threshold. Remaining risk: the four primary markets (AUDJPY, NZDJPY, AUDUSD, NZDUSD) are highly correlated, so '3 of 4 positive' is close to one observation, not three. The fri-minus-mon difference has a standard error of about 0.4 x sqrt(2/410) = 0.028 R, so the 0.03 R threshold is only about one standard error.
revisions: 1) Rationale and expectations: delete the 'three days of positive carry' / 'paid twice' claim. State that both arms cross exactly one 1x rollover (triple is Wednesday, in the engine and in Dukascopy prices), so net carry is about zero minus the 1% markup and the premium must come from price. Re-state the expected design avg R as a price-only premium after realistic weekend-edge costs: at least +0.02 R at sl_atr 1.5. 2) Cost statement: replace 'about 0.01 R' with an estimate from the actual Friday 20:00 UTC and Monday 00:00 UTC spreads, roughly 3-4 pips round trip including commission, 0.015-0.03 R. Report gross (before spread/commission) and net R for every arm, and report the mean entry and exit spread for each arm, so the fri/mon comparison can be read net of the spread difference. 3) Exit rule: X = the first H1 bar whose OPEN time (m.ts) is at or after exit_utc on D_exit, i.e. F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, [D_exit], hh, mm). Skip the trade if m.ts[X] is more than 60 minutes after the target (the max_bars net then does not apply). Set exit_long[X-1] = True when X-1 > S, so the close happens at the open of the bar starting at exit_utc. 4) Kill rule (4): the hard gate (check avg R > 0 over all check years) stays. 'Positive with 2020 removed' is an extra requirement, not a substitute. Also report 2015-08, 2020-03 and 2024-08 (holdout, at promotion only) weekend trades individually. 5) Control kill rule (2): keep the >= 0.03 R threshold and also report the t of the paired fri-minus-mon difference per market. Pre-register that the difference must be positive on at least 3 of the 4 AUD/NZD markets at the chosen combination, so one market cannot carry it. 6) Reduce max_bars to 24 for both arms. 80 H1 bars would let a missed Monday exit run to Wednesday and cross the triple rollover, mixing in exactly the carry the control is meant to exclude.
notes_for_builder: Follow the oracle pattern (strategies/oracle/m3_usd_bid.py) for clock times. Entry: for each UTC date D with weekday == entry_day (Fri = 4, Mon = 0 via F.weekday), ei = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, [D], eh, em). Require m.ts[ei] - (D + entry_utc) <= max_delay (60 min on H1) and ei >= 1. sig = ei - 1; entry_long[sig] = True, entry_type 0, valid_bars 1. sl_dist[sig] = p['sl_atr'] * atr[ei], where atr = daily.to_bars(F.atr_prev(daily, 20)); skip if not finite or <= 0. tp_dist NaN. Exit: D_exit = D + 3 days for 'fri', D + 1 day for 'mon'. xi = F.first_bar_at_or_after(m, [D_exit], xh, xm). Require xi < m.n, xi - 1 > sig and m.ts[xi] - (D_exit + exit_utc) <= 60 min. Then exit_long[xi - 1] = True, max_bars[sig] = 24 as a safety net. Do NOT use 'first bar whose close >= exit_utc' (that exits one hour early). Note that a Monday 00:00 exit target can be preceded by Sunday-evening UTC bars (the market opens Sun 21:00/22:00 UTC); first_bar_at_or_after on the Monday date handles that correctly. Read every grid key from p (entry_day, entry_utc, exit_utc, sl_atr) and put all of them in PARAMS. Longs only on every market; no side logic needed. Do not filter on anything else (no vol filter, no rate filter): the hypothesis is unconditional. Loop over dates, not bars.
